findings_qualitative.value: SFE' increases smoothly with LIR from normal galaxies to ULIRGs, with no bimodal jump

claims.hypothesis: SFE shows a bimodal jump between normal SFGs and starbursts
claims.experiment: Combined VALES ALMA and new APEX/SEPIA LIRG samples, compared SFE vs LIR and sSFR/sSFRms with literature
claims.result: SFE' is constant up to LIR~1e11 then increases smoothly; steep jump at sSFR/sSFRms>3 not seen

evidence.quote: we find a smooth transition of the SFE instead of a steep jump from the normal SFGs to the ULIRGs.

claims.hypothesis: Scatter in SFE is controlled by alpha_CO, gas fraction and size
claims.experiment: Compared SFE with alpha_CO and gas-to-dust, gas radius, and gas fraction scalings
claims.result: SFE anti-correlates with CO radius, slope about -0.6 ± 0.04 for ALMA-resolved galaxies
claims.finding: alpha_CO uncertainty, gas fraction and size drive scatter

evidence.quote: the main parameters controlling the scatter of the global SFE versus LIR correlation are: the assumed α CO conversion factor, the gas fraction and the physical size of the galaxies.

why_this_data.value: SEPIA Band-5 is the only southern instrument able to detect CO(2-1) at z=0.1-0.2

evidence.quote: SEPIA Band-5 is the only instrument that is able to detect CO ( J = 2–1) at redshifts from 0.1 to 0.2 in the Southern hemisphere.

limitations_admitted.value: APEX beam (~35") may include close counterparts; CO(2-1)/(1-0) ratio and alpha_CO assumptions add systematic uncertainty

evidence.quote: We expect this systematic variation will affect our result by 0.3 dex at most.
